Dennis Maldonado , Adversarial Engineer at LARES Consulting Follow Published on Aug 6, 2016 Pre-auth SYSTEM RCE on Windows Is more common than you think ---- With minimal to no effort, we can gain SYSTEM level access to hundreds, if not, thousands of machines on the internet [remotely]. No, this is not a new super 1337 exploit and no this is not even a new technique. No super fancy website with poorly designed logo is necessary, there is nothing new here. Tim and Dennis have discovered that something only stupid sysadmins would do turns out to be much more prevalent than expected. What starts off as a sysadmin's innocent attempt to fix an issue, turns into complete compromise of entire servers/workstations with no effort needed from the attacker. Tim and Dennis will discuss how we came to this realization and explain how we automated looking for these issues in order to find hundreds of vulnerable machines over the internet. Tim and Dennis explain the tool developed for automation, provide statistics discovered from our research, and go over ways to protect yourself from falling victim to the issue. ... Sticky Keys to the Kingdom PRE-AUTH SYSTEM RCE ON WINDOWS IS MORE COMMON THAN YOU THINK DENNIS MALDONADO & TIM MCGUFFIN LARES 2. About Us \xe2\x80\xa2 Dennis Maldonado \xe2\x80\xa2 Adversarial Engineer \xe2\x80\x93 LARES Consulting \xe2\x80\xa2 Founder \xe2\x80\xa2 Houston Locksport \xe2\x80\xa2 Houston Area Hackers Anonymous (HAHA) \xe2\x80\xa2 Tim McGuffin \xe2\x80\xa2 RedTeam Manager \xe2\x80\x93 LARES Consulting \xe2\x80\xa2 10-year DEFCON Goon \xe2\x80\xa2 DEFCON CTF Participant \xe2\x80\xa2 Former CCDCTeam Coach www.lares.com 3. History \xe2\x80\xa2 \xe2\x80\x9cHow to ResetWindows Passwords\xe2\x80\x9d websites \xe2\x80\xa2 Replace sethc.exe or utilman.exe with cmd.exe \xe2\x80\xa2 Reboot, Press Shift 5x orWIN+U \xe2\x80\xa2 net user (username) (password) \xe2\x80\xa2 Login! \xe2\x80\xa2 Nobody ever cleans up after themselves \xe2\x80\xa2 Can be used as a backdoor/persistence method \xe2\x80\xa2 NoWindows Event Logs are generated when backdoor is executed 4. Implementation \xe2\x80\xa2 Binary Replacement \xe2\x80\xa2 Replace any of the accessibility tool binaries \xe2\x80\xa2 Requires elevated rights \xe2\x80\xa2 Registry (Debugger Method) \xe2\x80\xa2 HKLMSoftwareMicrosoftWindows NTCurrentVersionImage File Execution Optionssethc.exe \xe2\x80\xa2 Debugger REG_SZ C:WindowsSystem32cmd.exe \xe2\x80\xa2 Requires elevated rights 5. Windows Accessibility Tools Binary Description How to access C:WindowsSystem32sethc.exe Accessibility shortcut keys Shift 5 times C:WindowsSystem32Utilman.exe Utility Manager Windows Key + U C:WindowsSystem32osk.exe On-Screen Keyboard Locate the option on the screen using the mouse C:WindowsSystem32Magnify.exe Magnifier Windows Key + [Equal Sign] C:WindowsSystem32Narrator.exe Narrator Windows Key + Enter C:WindowsSystem32DisplaySwitch.exe Display Switcher Windows Key + P C:WindowsSystem32AtBroker.exe Manages switching of apps between desktops Have osk.exe, Magnify.exe, or Narrator.exe open then lock the computer. AtBroker.exe will be executed upon locking and unlocking 6. Limitations \xe2\x80\xa2 Elevated access or offline system required \xe2\x80\xa2 Replacing binary must be Digitally Signed \xe2\x80\xa2 Replacing binary must exist in System32 \xe2\x80\xa2 Replacing binary must exist inWindows \xe2\x80\x9cProtected File\xe2\x80\x9d list \xe2\x80\xa2 You can\xe2\x80\x99t use any old Binary, but you can cmd.exe /c file.bat 7. Background \xe2\x80\xa2 While working with an Incident ResponseTeam: \xe2\x80\xa2 Uncovered dozens of vulnerable hosts via file checks \xe2\x80\xa2 Identification was done from the filesystem side \xe2\x80\xa2 Missed the debugger method \xe2\x80\xa2 Missed any unmanaged boxes \xe2\x80\xa2 Needed a network-based scanner 8. Background \xe2\x80\xa2 We wanted to write out own network-based tool \xe2\x80\xa2 Started down the JavaRDP/Python Path \xe2\x80\xa2 Ran across @ztgrace\xe2\x80\x99s PoC script, Sticky Keys Hunter \xe2\x80\xa2 It worked, and was a great starting point \xe2\x80\xa2 Similar to \xe2\x80\x9cPeepingTom\xe2\x80\x9d \xe2\x80\xa2 Opens a Remote Desktop connection \xe2\x80\xa2 Sends keyboard presses \xe2\x80\xa2 Saves screenshot to a file \xe2\x80\xa2 To do list including automatic command prompt detection and multi-threading 9. Our Solution \xe2\x80\x93 Sticky Key Slayer \xe2\x80\xa2 Parallelized scanning of multiple hosts \xe2\x80\xa2 Automated command prompt detection \xe2\x80\xa2 Detailed logging \xe2\x80\xa2 Error handling \xe2\x80\xa2 Performance improvements \xe2\x80\xa2 Bash 10. DEMO VIDEO: HTTPS://WWW.YOUTUBE.COM/WATCH?V=JY4HG4A1FYI 11. Tools Usage \xe2\x80\xa2 ./stickyKeysSlayer.sh -v -j 8 -t 10 targetlist.txt \xe2\x80\xa2 -v \xe2\x80\xa2 Verbose output \xe2\x80\xa2 -j <num_of_jobs> \xe2\x80\xa2 Jobs to run (defaults to 1) \xe2\x80\xa2 -t <time_in_seconds> \xe2\x80\xa2 Timeout in seconds (defaults to 30 seconds) \xe2\x80\xa2 targetlist.txt \xe2\x80\xa2 Hosts list delimited by line 12. Limitations \xe2\x80\xa2 Ties up a LinuxVM while scanning \xe2\x80\xa2 Needed for window focus and screenshotting \xe2\x80\xa2 Will not alert on anything that is not cmd.exe \xe2\x80\xa2 Ran across taskmgr.exe, mmc.exe, other custom applications 13. Statistics \xe2\x80\xa2 On a large Business ISP: \xe2\x80\xa2 Over 100,000 boxes scanned \xe2\x80\xa2 About 571 Command Prompts \xe2\x80\xa2 1 out of 175 \xe2\x80\xa2 All types of Institutions \xe2\x80\xa2 Educational Institutions \xe2\x80\xa2 Law Offices \xe2\x80\xa2 Manufacturing Facilities \xe2\x80\xa2 Gaming companies \xe2\x80\xa2 Etc\xe2\x80\xa6 14. Recommendations \xe2\x80\xa2 Remediation \xe2\x80\xa2 Delete or replace the affected file (sethc.exe, utilman.exe, \xe2\x80\xa6) \xe2\x80\xa2 sfc.exe /scannnow \xe2\x80\xa2 Remove the affected registry entry \xe2\x80\xa2 Treat this as an indicator of compromise \xe2\x80\xa2 Prevention and Detection \xe2\x80\xa2 Restrict local administrative access \xe2\x80\xa2 Enable full disk encryption \xe2\x80\xa2 Network LevelAuthentication for Remote Desktop Connection \xe2\x80\xa2 End point monitoring \xe2\x80\xa2 Netflow analysis 15. Tool Release \xe2\x80\xa2 Code is on Github \xe2\x80\xa2 https://github.com/linuz/Sticky-Keys-Slayer \xe2\x80\xa2 Contribute \xe2\x80\xa2 Report Issues \xe2\x80\xa2 Send us feedback \xe2\x80\xa2 Slides \xe2\x80\xa2 http://www.slideshare.net/DennisMaldonado5/sticky-keys- to-the-kingdom \xe2\x80\xa2 DemoVideo \xe2\x80\xa2 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jy4hg4a1FYI www.lares.com 16. Dennis Maldonado , Adversarial Engineer at LARES Consulting Follow Published on Aug 6, 2016 Pre-auth SYSTEM RCE on Windows Is more common than you think ---- With minimal to no effort, we can gain SYSTEM level access to hundreds, if not, thousands of machines on the internet [remotely].
No super fancy website with poorly designed logo is necessary, there is nothing new here.
Tim and Dennis have discovered that something only stupid sysadmins would do turns out to be much more prevalent than expected.
What starts off as a sysadmin's innocent attempt to fix an issue, turns into complete compromise of entire servers/workstations with no effort needed from the attacker.
Tim and Dennis explain the tool developed for automation, provide statistics discovered from our research, and go over ways to protect yourself from falling victim to the issue. ...
